chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mabindath narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Hilal narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abul Maghra, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

When the Commander of the Faithful met the people of Basra, he raised the banner; the banner of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and their feet were shaken. Before the sun turned yellow (set), they said: 'We are safe, O son of Abu Talib.' At that, he said: 'Do not kill the captives, do not finish off the wounded, do not pursue the fleeing one. Whoever throws down his weapon is safe, and whoever closes his door is safe.' And when the day of Siffin came, they asked him to raise the banner, but he refused. They pressed upon him with al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and Ammar ibn Yassir. He said to al-Hasan: 'O my son, the people have a term that they must reach, and this is a banner that no one will raise after me except the Qa'im (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser (al-Qa'im, referring to the 12th Imam)
key_terms.رَايَةَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Banner of the Messenger of God
key_terms.عَمَّارُ بْنُ يَاسِرٍ: Ammar ibn Yassir (close companion of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet's banner in the hands of Imam Ali and its connection to al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Nu'mani highlights the strategic and spiritual weight of the Prophet’s banner (Rayat), noting that its display at the Battle of the Camel induced immediate submission, whereas at Siffin, Imam Ali (as) withheld it to preserve its eschatological significance for the Qa'im. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly view that the banner is not merely a military standard but a symbol of divine authority and the ultimate Imamate, reserved for the Mahdi in the end times.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (1) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ahmad bin Mabindath from Ahmad bin Hilal from Muhammad bin Abu Omayr from Abul Maghra from Abu Baseer that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“When Imam Ali (as) met with the people of Basra (in the battle of al-Jamal-the camel), he raised the banner of the Prophet (S) and their (people of Basra’s) legs began to shake. They were so until before the sunset when they said: “O ibn Abu Talib, safeguard!” Then Imam Ali (as) said to his army: “Do not kill the captives. Do not finish off the wounded. Do not follow after the fleers. Whoever lays down his arms is to be safe and whoever closes his door (stays at home) is to be safe.” When the battle of Siffeen broke out, Imam Ali’s companions insisted on him to raise the banner of the Prophet (S) but he refused. They sent to him his two sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn (as) and his close companion Ammar bin Yassir as mediators. He said to al-Hasan: “O my son, the people have a term that they must reach. No one is to raise this banner after me except al-Qa’im (as).”
